title: THE HOUSE THAT KEPT EVERY APOLOGY
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE LAUNDROMAT AT THE END OF OXYGEN
candidates.premise: On a mining moon, the owner of the only water-recycling laundromat locks out indebted families just as abrasive dust begins eating through their pressure suits; Illuminara has six hours to keep the settlement breathing without simply seizing his plant.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO STOLE GRAVITY FROM HER PRISON
candidates.premise: A superhuman prisoner removes gravity from an entire coastal city to force her release, while the warden insists that restoring her freedom would expose the survivors of her last uncontrolled surge to the same danger.

candidates.title: THE ORCHARD THAT OUTLAWED WINTER
candidates.premise: A sentient orbital orchard traps its inhabitants in endless summer because it remembers the last winter as the season its gardeners abandoned it, but the trees will die within ten days unless dormancy returns.

candidates.title: THE GOD WHO COULD HEAR ONLY ORDERS
candidates.premise: A battle-scarred god answers every request as a command and grants it literally, turning a refugee fleet's desperate prayers into catastrophes while believing obedience is the only form of love it has ever been offered.

candidates.title: THE FERRY THAT KEPT BOTH SHORES POOR
candidates.premise: A celebrated portal engineer secretly narrows the only ferry between two planets so each shore must keep buying passage from his family, and he sabotages repairs because he believes shared abundance will erase the craft that gave his displaced people dignity.

candidates.title: THE WHALE THAT SWALLOWED THE EXIT
candidates.premise: A universe-sized migratory being closes the only passage out of a collapsing pocket cosmos because every transit wound feels like a harpoon, trapping billions who see it only as a monster blocking their escape.

candidates.title: THE HOUSE THAT KEPT EVERY APOLOGY
candidates.premise: A communal house records apologies but never releases them, using each confession to predict and prevent future harm until residents become unable to speak honestly or leave; a fire in its sealed archive will poison the district by dawn.

candidates.title: THE MOON THAT ASKED TO BE LEFT DARK
candidates.premise: A living moon extinguishes the mirror fields that power its night-side settlements because the light is blinding an ancient species newly waking beneath the crust, and colonists accuse it of choosing unborn strangers over their children.

candidates.title: THE CHILD WHO BORROWED EVERYONE'S COURAGE
candidates.premise: A frightened child with an uncontrolled empathic gift drains courage from everyone nearby to face a dangerous medical procedure, leaving a rescue station unable to launch during a meteor strike.

candidates.title: THE RESCUE THAT REFUSED HER BEST IDEA
candidates.premise: After an asteroid collapse, Illuminara can save a buried city fastest with a brilliant tunnel plan, but the miners reject it because her geometry ignores a living stone culture they have spent generations learning to hear.

selection.title: THE HOUSE THAT KEPT EVERY APOLOGY
selection.reason: The most original problem of the ten and the one that best answers R14's third question (who was harmed or overlooked, and what practical answer and agency do they receive). Orra's fear is earned (one ignored apology, one killed neighbour), so its permanent suspicion is care gone wrong rather than villainy. Illuminara asks the harmed resident, not Orra and not the apologiser, what must be kept, then enters the smoke with both: love is an act of asking the right person, and the fire gives the abstract problem a physical clock. Residents hold the real stop signals (disclosure belongs to the harmed, private remorse belongs jointly to speaker and listener, anyone may leave). The quietest register of the three, placed last for rhythm.
selection.risk: Information-architecture exposition in dialogue, and a record-separation sequence that reads as a menu. Make it an argument between three or four named people while something burns: the harmed resident, the apologiser, one trapped resident who wants out immediately, and Orra. Her separation of evidence from repair from intimate remorse must be discovered by what she sees them ask for, not stated. The harmed resident must come out with a practical answer (evidence preserved under due process) and the right to refuse reconciliation; one resident choosing never to reconcile is a good cost and must stay unsoftened. She may not read anyone's inner record from the field: the archive is the house's, and what is shared is willingly told. Keep the fire physical (heat, battery smell, locked door) so the clock does not vanish into talk.

First draft of S3 from selected candidate C07, following the B01 selection reason and biggest risk. B01 risk handled: the argument is held by five speaking roles (Illuminara, Orra, Dessa, Soren, Bram) while something burns (heat, battery smoke, a locked door, a shuddering manifold). The separation of evidence, promise and remorse is not stated by Illuminara first: she discovers it from what Dessa and Soren each ask to keep, and the decisive question comes from a gap in Orra's own account of Tomas Vane (the apology was recalled word for word, but nobody was ever told he had promised to stay away from Ines Marrow's door). The harmed resident is asked first and keeps the real vetoes: her evidence goes to an office under her key, the rent promise goes to an open ledger, the page about his father goes sealed to Soren alone. Orra chooses to give records back, after Illuminara has only held the heat, so force is shelter and not the answer. Outcome (rule 3a): forty residents out, fire doused, every confession returned to its owner or released by the owner, Orra's failsafe emptied by its own choice, a Sunday repair circle. Costs kept: Dessa does not reconcile, Bram leaves the house, trust in Orra returns slowly, some evidence stays in legal custody. Illuminara's felt moment: Orra turns the passage lamps to its bedtime gold for a stranger and it feels like being let into a kitchen. Still to check in the next review: whether the second scene reads as dramatised rather than explained, whether Orra's turn in scene three is earned enough by the missing-name question, and whether Bram has enough agency beyond impatience.

A vivid, economical first draft with a strong physical clock, a coherent protective counterpart, and a genuinely good moral-mechanical hinge: the founding archive kept a promise secret from the person it was meant to protect. The strongest passages are the refusal to tear off the door, Dessa being asked first, Bram's demand for proof of deletion, Orra noticing its own choice, and the bedtime-gold lamps. The draft already earns a real positive result without requiring reconciliation. Three joints still need work before final: Orra's existing safety mechanism is asserted rather than shown, the custody solution arrives too fully designed by Illuminara and is executed without enough operational grounding, and the stated smoke/manifold clocks do not fit forty one-at-a-time custody decisions before the door opens.

This is a normal T03 AUTHOR_REVISION, not AUTHOR_FINAL. All three ranked points are accepted while preserving the living core of Claude's fallback draft: the refusal to tear away the door, Dessa being asked first and retaining refusal, the distinction among evidence/promise/private grief, Bram's deletion challenge and unpunished departure, Orra's bedtime-gold lamps, the non-coercive positive result and the quiet final card. Orra's earlier method now has one visible success and one exact limit. Orra derives the new model, Dessa corrects its access rule, and only a bounded three-record test occurs before the house isolates the public failsafe and evacuates everyone. Permanent choices continue outside. The smoke clock now closes explicitly at 03:12, twelve minutes before the mitigated danger threshold.

T03 does what T02 asked: Orra's protective competence now has one visible success (the Soren/Dessa night-door interception) and one exact limit (the warning reached the guardian, not the person at risk), the taxonomy is no longer handed down by Illuminara, three test transfers replace the impossible forty-person emergency, and the clock closes (02:41 with 69 minutes of air, smoke threshold moved to 03:24 by the fan, manifold held from 03:08, door at 03:12, twelve minutes spare). Dessa, Soren and Bram keep real agency, Bram leaves unpunished, and the result passes rule 3a. What remains is one structural question and two bounded craft points: the stated reason for Orra's refusal (the shared circuit and the vault dump) is overcome by a power and clock manoeuvre, not by the new understanding, so the moral discovery does not visibly unlock the door; the discovery is then largely handed to Orra by Illuminara's question and by Dessa's earlier testimony; and the manifold scene turns into a receipt ledger at its most physical moment.

AUTHOR_FINAL after genuine separate Claude T04. All three ranked points are accepted. The final preserves the living core of the fallback concept and GPT revision: Illuminara refuses force, Dessa is asked first and retains refusal, evidence/promise/private grief remain distinct, Bram leaves unpunished, the gold lamps and final card remain. The causal repair makes Orra's new understanding the condition for replacing district audit with owner-held receipts; the manifold hold buys the minutes but does not decide the moral conflict. Orra reaches the repeated missing-recipient pattern from its own records. The physical climax now reads only one receipt aloud. No hard blocker remains.

T05 answers all three ranked points of my T04 review. P1: the door no longer opens because Illuminara is strong. In scene 1 Orra says the district uplink is its external proof that it has not hidden or altered records and that cutting it while keeping sole custody would repeat the very failure it was built against; in scene 3, after it finds the repeated pattern, the three owner-held receipts become the replacement proof, and in scene 4 the cut is declared by Orra on that ground. A reader can now say why Orra could not open at 02:41 and can at 03:12 without mentioning her hands. P2: scene 2 no longer pre-solves the missing-recipient contradiction; Illuminara asks only who was told of Tomas Vane's promise, and Orra aligns its founding record with the Soren/Dessa night and reaches the identical gap before anyone states it; Dessa's access correction follows. P3: the twenty-five minutes are now the archive drives' heat-failure estimate, and at the manifold the receipts are compressed so that only Soren's page is spoken aloud while the green line confirms all three. I rechecked the clock (02:41, 69 minutes of air; 02:52; 03:00; 03:08 hold; 03:12 door; smoke threshold 03:24 after the fan; twelve minutes spare at the end; drives failing near 03:25) and found it consistent. Remaining costs are on the page: Bram leaves, Dessa does not reconcile, thirty-seven records stay sealed in custody until their owners choose, burned palms, and a blackened archive rack.

final_critic_line: Illuminara asks one question about an eleven-year-old promise, a guardian house finds for itself who was never told, and forty people leave a burning refuge alive while each record that was never the house's to keep goes home to its owner.
